analysis.title: Dividends shine as tech cools (Weekly Market Directions)
key_insights: Amundi says confidence in the AI theme has weakened in recent weeks. The MSCI World Technology Index gave back all of the previous month's gains, likely on mixed corporate earnings and renewed concerns about AI-related capital expenditure.
Amundi argues markets have moved past the phase where a mention of an AI roll-out excited investors. Investors now want evidence of cash generation and profitability from the large AI investments.
The MSCI World High Dividend Yield Index gained 8.0% in H2 versus 0.2% for the tech index. Consumer staples, healthcare and utilities held up as the broader market fell.
Amundi sees diversification opportunities in more attractively valued sectors with strong, stable businesses, and expects companies that consistently return cash to shareholders to stay in demand.
Global equities came under pressure in the week to 23 October, led by a reversal in technology stocks that spread more broadly.
Bond yields fell in some countries, such as the US, on safe-haven demand. Fiscal concerns pushed yields higher in other countries (France, Italy and the UK 10-year yields rose on the week).
Oil was affected by a flare-up in Middle East tensions. Gold declined on concerns that persistent inflation could prompt central banks to raise interest rates.

Eurozone composite PMI (preliminary October) fell to 51.9 from 53.1 in September, below expectations, with services and manufacturing both slowing. Readings remain above 50 and investor and consumer confidence weakened.

US initial jobless claims fell to 194,000 in the week ending 17 October, below expectations. September housing starts fell to an annualised 1.22 million, sharply below forecasts and down from the prior month.
Japan's core inflation (excluding fresh food and energy) rose to 2.4% in September, above expectations and up from August. A 20-year JGB auction drew record demand.

sector_views.rationale: They held up well while the broader market fell and offer diversification through more attractively valued sectors with stable businesses.
The MSCI World Technology Index gave back the previous month's gains on mixed earnings and AI capex concerns, and markets want evidence of cash flow.

Sharply below forecasts and down from the prior month, so higher borrowing costs continue to weigh on residential construction.
